# Ospia

> Ospia is an AI-native Hospital Operating System for Indian hospitals: a digital
> workforce of AI agents that runs admissions, billing, claims, pharmacy and
> inventory alongside hospital staff, under an autonomy level the hospital sets
> per task, with every decision explainable and replayable.

Ospia is early. We work with design-partner hospitals and do not publish customer
counts or outcome figures we have not earned.

## Start here

- [What is an AI Hospital Operating System? | Ospia](https://ospia.in/ai-hospital-operating-system.html): An AI-native Hospital Operating System runs a hospital's clinical, financial and operational work through governed AI agents on one unified database. What it is, how it differs from a legacy HIS/HMS, and why Indian hospitals need one.
- [Platform — Ospia Hospital Operating System](https://ospia.in/platform.html): The Ospia platform: ten capability pillars, the task and intent registry, the rules and policy engine, permanent event history and the insight surface.
- [AI Workforce — twelve digital employees | Ospia](https://ospia.in/ai-workforce.html): Ospia's AI workforce: twelve digital employees with defined responsibilities, permissions, KPIs and escalation rules — each at an autonomy level the hospital configures from L0 to L4.
- [Architecture — Ospia Hospital Operating System](https://ospia.in/architecture.html): Ospia's architecture: a modular monolith with fully isolated domains, per-module schemas, a durable event backbone, and six CI-enforced architectural gates.
- [Compliance — ABDM, DPDP, NMC, NABH, GST | Ospia](https://ospia.in/compliance.html): How Ospia meets Indian healthcare regulation: ABDM and ABHA, DPDP consent ledger, NMC prescribing rules enforced at write time, NABH evidence, GST e-invoicing, plus HIPAA readiness and ISO roadmap.
- [Security — Ospia Hospital Operating System](https://ospia.in/security.html): Ospia security in detail: zero trust, multi-tenancy and data isolation, encryption, key management, hash-chained audit, backup and disaster recovery, secure SDLC, penetration testing and the compliance roadmap.
